topics: reading: The legend of the Lady of the Lake (a folk tale)
narrative: the past simple and the past continuous
linkers: when, while, as soon as

paper:
Once upon a time, in a small village between two mountains, there lived a poor fisherman called Hamid. One evening, while he was fishing in the lake, he heard a soft voice. He looked around but saw nobody. Suddenly, a golden fish jumped out of the water and spoke to him: "Please let me go, and I will help your village."

Hamid was kind, so he put the fish back into the water. The next morning, as soon as the villagers woke up, they found that the dry fields near the lake were green again. From that day on, the village never suffered from drought. When people asked Hamid about the miracle, he only smiled and said, "Kindness always comes back to you."

Part One: Reading (15 points)

A. Comprehension (08 pts)

1. The text is: a) a biography b) a tale c) an e-mail. Justify with one expression from the text.

2. Put the events in the right order: a) The fields became green. b) Hamid heard a voice. c) The fish asked Hamid to free it. d) Hamid put the fish back into the water.

3. Answer: a) What was Hamid doing when he heard the voice? b) What lesson does the story teach?

4. Who or what do the underlined words refer to? "he heard a soft voice" ; "they found…"

B. Text exploration (07 pts)

1. Find in the text the opposite of: rich ≠ … ; wet ≠ … ; loud ≠ …

2. Join each pair of sentences with the linker given: a) Hamid was walking home. He met an old man. (while) b) The sun rose. The villagers went to the fields. (as soon as)

3. Give the past simple of: hear – find – say – put.

Part Two: Written expression (05 points)

Write a short tale (10–12 lines) that teaches a lesson (honesty, patience, helping others…). Start with "Once upon a time…" and use the past simple, the past continuous and linkers.
